purpose: A bank of 32 hardware spinlocks. On a bus read of lock i the module returns the lock's old value and sets it (an atomic test-and-set). A write to lock i clears it. A separate read-only address returns all 32 lock bits.

flows.name: acquire (test-and-set read of one lock)
flows.value: lock bit i: its old value is returned to the reader and it is set to '1' in the same clock edge

path.edge: SOURCES lock_q (lock_q(i) <= not bus_req_i.rw; a read, rw='0', stores '1')
DERIVES_FROM bus_req_i.rw; storage=edge (holds the lock across cycles)
SOURCES bus_rsp_o.data (old value, same edge as the set at line 45)
SOURCES bus_rsp_o.data (masks the response to bit i)
DERIVES_FROM lock_q, sel; storage=edge; leaves the module

controls.edge: GATES lock_q (addr(7)='0' selects the per-lock region)

controls.decided_by: bus_req_i.addr(6 downto 2) compared with the generate index i, line 51 (sel GATED_BY bus_req_i.addr, sel occ 3)

controls.edge: GATES bus_rsp_o.data (addr(7)='0' picks line 68, else line 70)

path.edge: constant driver (others => '0'): a write returns zero

flows.name: status read (all locks, no side effect)

path.edge: constant driver '0' (no error is ever signalled)

conceptual_assets.name: lock state (32 mutual-exclusion bits)

C.why: Line 70 returns all 32 lock bits to any reader when addr(7)='1', with no check, and no line treats occupancy as secret. Knowing which locks are held does not let a reader take or break one. (Occupancy as a timing side channel is a hypothesis, not a mechanism here.)

I.why: Any write that reaches a lock address clears lock_q(i) (not rw = '0'). The condition on line 44 tests only stb, addr(7) and sel(i), so any master can release a lock another master holds. Mutual exclusion then fails.

A.why: A read sets lock_q(i) to '1'. Only a write (line 45) or a reset (line 42) clears it. There is no owner and no timeout, so a master that reads all 32 lock addresses and never writes blocks every other master's acquire forever.

U.why: The update condition accepts every transaction. The request record declares privilege, source and debug fields (line 22), but no line reads them (map: declaration occurrence only, no edges). bus_rsp_o.err is fixed at '0' (line 64), so a foreign release or acquire is never flagged.

conceptual_assets.attack_effect: A rogue or buggy master writes a lock address and clears lock_q(i) through line 45 while the owner is in its critical section. The next acquire read at line 68 then returns '0' to a second master, and two masters hold the same lock. Or the master sets all 32 bits and keeps them, so every acquire at line 68 returns '1' forever.

conceptual_assets.name: lock-select decision (which lock a transaction acts on)

C.why: It comes from the requester's own address. Nothing about it is secret.

I.why: sel(i) is the only per-lock enable of the set/clear on line 45 and the mask of the acquire result on line 68. If sel is corrupted (for example by a fault), the wrong lock is set or cleared, or another lock's state is returned. The requester then believes it holds lock i when it does not.

A.why: It is a combinational decode (logic with no stored state) that is always produced. It has no stall path.

U.why: No mode or override forces sel. It depends only on addr(6 downto 2).

conceptual_assets.attack_effect: A glitched sel on line 44 lets an acquire read set a different lock bit from the one returned on line 68. The master enters lock i's critical section while lock i stays free for others.

conceptual_assets.name: acquire outcome (old state of the requested lock, returned by the test-and-set read)

C.why: It goes only to the requester, who is entitled to it.

I.why: The requester decides whether it owns lock i from this bit. Line 68 and the set on line 45 sample lock_q on the same clock edge, and that is what makes the test-and-set atomic. A '0' returned while lock_q(i) was '1' would admit a second owner.

A.why: ack follows stb one cycle later with no stall path, so the outcome is always delivered.

U.why: The status region (addr(7)='1', line 70) reads without setting, but line 44 requires addr(7)='0' for any update. No mode changes what line 68 returns.

conceptual_assets.attack_effect: If the value on line 68 were forced or corrupted to '0', two masters would each believe they had acquired lock i. It is realised by lock_q and sel. Its exit, bus_rsp_o.data, is excluded by the bus-record rule.

primary.concept: lock state; also the source of the acquire outcome (line 68) and of the status read (line 70)
primary.edge: storage=edge (kind register); DERIVES_FROM bus_req_i.rw at occ 3; GATED_BY bus_req_i.addr, bus_req_i.stb, sel at occ 3; RESET_BY rstn_i at occ 2; SOURCES bus_rsp_o.data at occ 4; CARRIES bus_rsp_o.data at occ 5
primary.why: The only element that holds a lock across cycles. It is set by any read (line 45), cleared by any write (line 45) or by reset (line 42), and exported on lines 68 and 70. Its integrity and availability are the module's security properties, and neither is protected by any check (line 44).

primary.edge: GATED_BY bus_req_i.addr at occ 3 (line 51); GATES lock_q at occ 2 (line 44); SOURCES bus_rsp_o.data at occ 4 (line 68)
primary.why: Assigned the decision of which lock a transaction acts on (line 51). That decision is the per-bit enable of every lock update (line 44) and the mask that turns lock_q into the acquire result (line 68). It is the internal element that decides the value the bus record delivers, so Step 5 says to report it in place of the bus ports.

Reset: decides when, not what. Its effect (every lock released, line 42) is noted under hypotheses.

Field of the bus-transaction record. Its value is what lock_q stores (line 45), so lock_q is reported instead. It stays a control point in the flows.
Field of the bus-transaction record. Its lock-index part is decided into sel (line 51), which is reported instead. Its region bit addr(7) gates lines 44 and 67 and is listed as a flow control.

Field of the bus-response record and the exit of the lock state (lines 68, 70). Under Step 5 the internal elements that store and decide what it delivers (lock_q, sel) are reported instead. This conflicts with Step 4's 'report each exit' and is the least sure exclusion.
Field of the bus-response record. A registered copy of stb (line 63): handshake only, with no security value.
Field of the bus-response record. Constant '0' (line 64), so it carries no value to protect. That it is constant is part of the U answer.

hypotheses: Ownership enforcement. The SoC may expect only the lock owner, or only privileged software, to release a lock. This source has no such check (priv/src/debug are unused), so any enforcement must live outside it (a bus firewall or PMP). Nothing here proves it exists.
Lock occupancy as a side channel. The status read (line 70) shows any master which locks are held and when. Whether that timing is sensitive depends on the software.

Reset as an override. rstn_i clears every lock (line 42) and cuts short any response (line 61). If an untrusted agent can trigger this reset (a watchdog or software reset), it force-releases locks that other masters believe they hold. Who controls rstn_i is outside this source.
Address aliasing. addr(1 downto 0) and every bit above 7 are ignored (lines 44, 51, 67), so many addresses map to the same lock. Whether this matters depends on the SoC address decoder.
Byte enables are ignored (ben unused). A write of any width releases the lock.

map_assessment.used_for: Indexing all 21 elements and 31 relationship records. A self-check found 0 of 63 occurrences that disagreed with the source text, and every edge had its inverse record. The map gave: lock_q as the only register besides the response fields; the full data and control edge set around lock_q and bus_rsp_o.data; the fact that bus_req_i.data, ben, src, priv, debug, amo, amoop, lock and fence have only a declaration occurrence and no edges; and the constant drivers of err, data and lock_q. That last fact is how the missing ownership or privilege check (the U answer) was found.
map_assessment.insufficient_for: (1) The meaning of line 45: that a READ is the acquire (it stores not '0' = '1') and a write is the release. The edge says only that lock_q DERIVES_FROM rw. (2) That lines 45 and 68 sample lock_q on the same clock edge, which is what makes the test-and-set atomic. (3) The per-bit generate structure: sel(i) is compared with the loop constant i, and lock_q(i) is written under sel(i). (4) bus_req_i.addr is a single element, so addr(7) (region: lock or status) and addr(6 downto 2) (lock index) are mixed together, and the source was needed to tell them apart. (5) An absent check can only be inferred from empty edge lists; the map cannot state it. All five needed the source.
map_assessment.errors_found: No edge errors found. Two small issues. The functionality hint for bus_req_i.rw ('selecting read responses or write updates to locks') misses that reads also update locks: line 45 sets the lock on a read. The record-level bus_rsp_o has storage 'none' and only a RESET_BY edge, yet it is assigned in a clocked process (lines 61-70) and its fields are storage 'edge'.

process_notes: 1. Read the prompt, then the whole source (45 lines, 1 entity). 2. Indexed the map with Python (index_map.py): every element's occurrences, edges, storage and constant drivers. 3. Self-check (checks.py): occurrence text against the source lines (0/63 mismatches), edge ids and inverse records (31 records, 0 asymmetric), declaration-only elements. 4. Worked out the purpose and flows from the source: per-lock region (addr(7)='0', index addr(6:2)), where a read sets the lock and returns its old value, and a write clears it; status region (addr(7)='1'), which is read-only and returns all bits. 5. Traced each flow along map edges and confirmed every edge on its line. 6. Answered C/I/A/U from lines 44, 45, 51, 63, 64, 68 and 70. Where the map changed a decision: the empty edge lists of priv/src/debug turned the U answer from 'unknown' to 'yes, line 44 admits every master'. Where the source was needed instead of the map: the read-sets/write-clears meaning of 'not rw', the same-edge atomicity of lines 45 and 68, and the split of addr into region bit and index. Rule conflict: Step 4 (report each exit point) and Step 5 (replace bus-record ports with internal elements) disagree on bus_rsp_o.data. I applied Step 5, excluded it, and marked it least sure. No element was reported because of its name.
